main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating pattern of darker green clumps, light checkered tufts and scattered dark dots. It is terrain with no standing volume.
top_band: none - flat terrain texture, no standing object with top and front faces
evidence: Terrain ground tile: a seamless grass fill with no object body. The 3/4 contract (top band plus front face) does not apply to a ground patch. There is no side face and no front elevation, so nothing in this drawing violates the terrain kind.

style.evidence: The candidate uses about 4 green steps: base, light tuft, dark clump and dark dots. The clumps and checkered tufts add variation, but the pattern repeats mechanically every 5 tiles or so, giving a regular wallpaper look. The Beodeul grass reference has more varied tufts, soil grain and more organic irregularity. Large areas of the base green are flat between the motifs, and the per-tile colour count is lower than the reference. It reads as thinner and more patterned than the reference, so it fails.
